messages:
Sophia: quick update — ran a W-only INT8 (bitsandbytes / llm.int8) pass on multi-query workload (10k qps sim) against aurora13b. latency looks good but saw a quality delta on a few eval slices.

Ana: how big is the latency win?

Sophia: p50 ~18% lower, p95 ~12% lower on our p3 configs; throughput up ~1.6x. GPU token cost down ~40%.

Mike: what do the accuracy numbers look like? any catastrophic drops?

Sophia: overall qual drop is small, but one slice (math / chain-of-thought) has ~2.4% exact-match regression. convo & summarization slices are within noise.

Lee: did you check log-prob shifts or calibration?

Sophia: yes — avg log-prob drops slightly in the bad slice, and we see more short hallucinations on multi-step reasoning.

Ana: what quant config did you use? group size, special bnb flags?

Sophia: config we tried:
```json
{"quant_type":"llm.int8","bnb_config":{"zero_point":false,"use_double_quant":false},"group_size":256,"optimize_kernels":true,"batch_size":8}
```

Mike: tried smaller groups? GPTQ/AWQ comparisons?

Sophia: grouping=128 reduced the regression to ~1.8% but perf regressed slightly. haven't run AWQ/GPTQ yet — plan to compare.

Lee: ops notes: verify KV-cache key stability and layernorm behavior with weight-only quant. We had a cache mismatch once when layer folding was applied.

infra-bot: reminder: deploy checklist requires model metadata: tokenizer sha, model config, and explicit "w-only-int8" flag for routing.

Sophia: thinking about rollout policy: canary 5% traffic int8, route fallback for slices where eval delta > 1% to fp16. Also enable per-slice telemetry to auto-detect regressions.

Ana: if we see persistent regressions, try enabling mixed-precision fallback for FFN layers or fall back on a GPTQ-converted variant for the math slice.

Sophia: good idea. i'll queue a run to convert the offending layers with AWQ and compare accuracy vs throughput tonight.

eval-bot: uploaded results: /evals/int8/multiquery/2138765432_summary.csv — includes p50/p95, throughput, and slice deltas.

Mike: thanks. please also capture prompt-length distribution for the canary so we don't accidentally bias toward short-form.

Sophia: will do. scheduling a longer 5k-request canary tomorrow AM and pushing eval scripts + slice defs to /evals/int8-multq/. Will ping when ready. :rocket:

Ana: +1. can we also try TTL-based KV cache invalidation during canary to see cache sensitivity?

Sophia: yep, I'll add that to the runbook.

Mike: sounds good — let's sync 10am tomorrow to decide rollout or hold.

Sophia: added a calendar invite. thanks everyone!
